## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code contains the diagnosis module, not the GRU4Rec implementation. Diagnosis examines item embeddings and per-position sequence features exposed through ModelView. `log2feats(sequence)` supplies these features; `predict_score(features, items)` produces candidate logits. The model’s representation computation cannot be verified here. Final inference on left-padded histories must select the final nonpadding position; these probes instead score all positions with nonzero positive targets.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and accesses `item_emb`, `user_train`, `meta_data`, and `review_data`; histories and review data are stored but unused. The underlying module is available as `view.model`.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. The probe calls `eval()` and scores up to ten batches without gradients. Paired candidate IDs have shape `B × L × 2`.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`**: Samples at most 2,048 real-item embeddings with seed 42, excluding padding and reserved tokens. It normalizes vectors, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result using `(mean + 1)/2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 represents near-zero average cosine, not necessarily collapse.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`**: Mean and tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits over nonzero positive targets. Higher values suggest stronger separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`**: Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`**: Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`**: Counts low-margin and wrong-ranking positions and lists the top 20 metadata categories separately for positive and negative items.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, ablation, or sensitivity perturbation is performed. Random embedding subsampling estimates geometric alignment; supplied positive/negative pairs test training-position discrimination.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting a JSON interpretation with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog recommendation diversity, temporal sensitivity, or generalization. Margins depend on logit scale and sampled negatives. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists should remain empty. Empty margin samples return zeros, which must not be mistaken for healthy measurements.

Its [official implementation](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential) keeps trained GRU4Rec models fixed and compares original versus shuffled inference histories using HR@10, NDCG@10 and recommendation-list Jaccard@10. Effects vary sharply: reported GRU4Rec HR@10 changes include −25% on Beauty, −63% on MovieLens-20M and −7% on Yelp. This supports measuring both target accuracy and recommendation stability; weak accuracy changes alone do not establish that predictions are unchanged.

Recency is a related but distinct question. ## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code contains the diagnosis module, not the GRU4Rec implementation. Diagnosis examines item embeddings and per-position sequence features exposed through ModelView. `log2feats(sequence)` supplies these features; `predict_score(features, items)` produces candidate logits. The model’s representation computation cannot be verified here. Final inference on left-padded histories must select the final nonpadding position; these probes instead score all positions with nonzero positive targets.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and accesses `item_emb`, `user_train`, `meta_data`, and `review_data`; histories and review data are stored but unused. The underlying module is available as `view.model`.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. The probe calls `eval()` and scores up to ten batches without gradients. Paired candidate IDs have shape `B × L × 2`.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`**: Samples at most 2,048 real-item embeddings with seed 42, excluding padding and reserved tokens. It normalizes vectors, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result using `(mean + 1)/2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 represents near-zero average cosine, not necessarily collapse.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`**: Mean and tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits over nonzero positive targets. Higher values suggest stronger separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`**: Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`**: Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`**: Counts low-margin and wrong-ranking positions and lists the top 20 metadata categories separately for positive and negative items.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, ablation, or sensitivity perturbation is performed. Random embedding subsampling estimates geometric alignment; supplied positive/negative pairs test training-position discrimination.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting a JSON interpretation with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog recommendation diversity, temporal sensitivity, or generalization. Margins depend on logit scale and sampled negatives. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists should remain empty. Empty margin samples return zeros, which must not be mistaken for healthy measurements.
